classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught sketching procedure using intercepts, an exact point, growth or decay and the horizontal asymptote.

inlines.text: Sketch the graph of the following exponential functions.

answer.short: Increasing exponential through $(0,1)$ and $(1,2)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=0$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=2^0\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
At $x=1$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=2^1\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Sketch an increasing curve through $(0,1)$ and $(1,2)$. The horizontal asymptote is $y=0$. As $x\to-\infty$, $y\to0$; as $x\to\infty$, $y\to\infty$.

answer.short: Increasing exponential through $(0,1)$ and $(1,e)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=0$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=e^0\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
At $x=1$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=e^1\\y&=e\end{align*}$$
Since $e>1$, sketch an increasing curve through $(0,1)$ and $(1,e)$. The horizontal asymptote is $y=0$. As $x\to-\infty$, $y\to0$; as $x\to\infty$, $y\to\infty$.

answer.short: Decreasing exponential through $(0,1)$ and $(-1,3)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=0$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=3^0\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
At $x=-1$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=3^{-(-1)}\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
Sketch a decreasing curve through $(0,1)$ and $(-1,3)$. The horizontal asymptote is $y=0$. As $x\to\infty$, $y\to0$; as $x\to-\infty$, $y\to\infty$.

answer.short: Decreasing exponential through $(0,1)$ and $(-1,e)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=0$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=e^0\\y&=1\end{align*}$$
At $x=-1$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=e^{-(-1)}\\y&=e\end{align*}$$
Since $e>1$, the negative exponent gives decay. Sketch a decreasing curve through $(0,1)$ and $(-1,e)$. The horizontal asymptote is $y=0$. As $x\to\infty$, $y\to0$; as $x\to-\infty$, $y\to\infty$.

answer.short: Increasing exponential through $(0,2)$ and $\left(-1,\frac23\right)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=0$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=2(3^0)\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
At $x=-1$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=2(3^{-1})\\y&=\frac23\end{align*}$$
Sketch an increasing curve through $(0,2)$ and $\left(-1,\frac23\right)$. The horizontal asymptote is $y=0$. As $x\to-\infty$, $y\to0$; as $x\to\infty$, $y\to\infty$.

answer.short: Decreasing exponential through $(0,3)$ and $\left(1,\frac32\right)$, with horizontal asymptote $y=0$.
answer.worked:
At $x=0$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=3(2^0)\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
At $x=1$,
$$\begin{align*}y&=3(2^{-1})\\y&=\frac32\end{align*}$$
Sketch a decreasing curve through $(0,3)$ and $\left(1,\frac32\right)$. The horizontal asymptote is $y=0$. As $x\to\infty$, $y\to0$; as $x\to-\infty$, $y\to\infty$.
